rules: ONE daily card post. Slot = ISO week number mod 4 -> row of `rotation`, weekday Mon=0 -> column.
Monthly special: if today is a Saturday, no us_vs_uk in the last 28 days, and the month has no us_vs_uk yet, use us_vs_uk instead of the planned series.
how_company only if a candidate company has a NEWER reported quarter than the one in the log; otherwise use `fallbacks`.
trend only if a topic is clearly trending today and verifiable; otherwise use `fallbacks`.
Never the same series as yesterday. Never repeat a topic within 56 days. Never repeat a company until it reports a newer quarter.
Never post an unverified number. If a series cannot be verified today, pick the next fallback.
Stock Market Today is a separate task and does not count here.

how_company.name: How (company) makes money?
how_company.desc: Quarterly income-statement flow chart: revenue segments -> gross profit -> operating profit -> net income, with costs and tax. THE reference template (scripts/make_flow.py + video flow streaks).
how_company.how: Use scripts/make_flow.py exactly (data.json per the make_flow docstring in the old prompt: company, period, rev, cogs, opex, other, tax, prior{rev,gp,op,ni}, segments, other_label, cogs_name, opex_name, tax_name, source). Only when a company has reported a quarter NEWER than the one already charted (see log). Verify the numbers tie to the filing.
how_company.note: Charted so far: Nvidia (Q2 FY27), Apple (Q4 FY26). Earnings seasons: mid-Jan to Feb, mid-Apr to May, mid-Jul to Aug, mid-Oct to Nov; off-cycle reporters fill gaps.

country_vs_country.name: Country vs country
country_vs_country.desc: Two (sometimes three) countries compared on 4-6 relevant economic measures with one clear verdict per measure. Pick matchups people care about or are in the news.
forms: head-to-head split with big numbers and winner marker
scorecard of 5 mini bars with flags
country_vs_country.verify: Each number needs a named source and a year; same year for both countries; state units (PPP vs nominal). Prefer latest full-year data.

wave.name: Wave visual: 8-10 countries compared
wave.desc: A flowing 'wave' / ridge / ribbon style graphic comparing 8-10 countries on one statistic (the user's saved Instagram reference). If reference_style is missing, make the nicest clean wave: smooth sorted ribbon or stacked wave with flags at each country.
wave.reference_style: Not yet provided by the user. When the user sends the Instagram screenshot, update this entry and brand/feedback.
forms: smooth sorted wave line with flag markers
wave.verify: Same year and definition for every country; mark the highlighted country in red.

explained.name: Explained: Why are / Why do / What are
explained.desc: One sharp economic question answered visually in one card. Titles start with 'Why are...', 'Why do...' or 'What are...'. Over-simplified but correct.
forms: cause-and-effect chain of 3-4 boxes with a number each
explained.verify: Every claim needs a named source. Where economists disagree say 'one reason' not 'the reason'.
topics: Why are interest rates raised to fight inflation?
Why is the Swiss franc so strong?
Why are concert tickets so expensive?
Why is petrol cheaper in the US?
Why do rich countries have lower growth?
Why is gold at record highs?

who_owns.name: Who owns...?
who_owns.desc: Ownership breakdown of a famous company, asset or sector (shareholders, funds, families, governments).
forms: ranked list with logos replaced by coloured initials
sources: Bloomberg-style public holder lists via Yahoo Finance
who_owns.verify: Cross-check two sources and show the as-of date. Never state ownership of private individuals' wealth as fact unless published by a reliable source.
topics: Who owns the UK's water companies?
Who owns the UK's energy firms?
Who owns the big four banks in the UK?

how_business.name: How (business) makes money?
how_business.desc: A flow chart of a typical everyday business: what comes in, what goes out, profit, tax. Label clearly as 'typical / illustrative' unless sourced.
forms: pound/dollar split into coins as dot grid
how_business.verify: Use sourced typical margins (state source and year); label 'illustrative' for any estimate; never invent a precise figure.

how_finance.name: How (finance) works
how_finance.desc: Over-simplified visual explainer of a financial system idea (banks, central banks, markets).
forms: flow diagram with arrows and numbers
how_finance.verify: Simplify wording but keep the mechanism correct; show a worked example with round numbers.
topics: How interest rates move your mortgage
How a central bank prints money
How a stock exchange makes money

price_of.name: Price of... comparisons
price_of.desc: One item compared across countries or across time (a Big Mac, a pint, rent, a cinema ticket, a coffee).
price_of.verify: Same currency conversion date; state year; label crowdsourced data as such.
topics: Price of a pint in Europe
Cost of a coffee in 10 cities
Cost of a new iPhone by country
Price of a Netflix subscription by country
Average house price to income ratio

inflation_pocket.name: What £100 / $100 bought then vs now
inflation_pocket.desc: Purchasing power over time with simple items.
inflation_pocket.verify: State the years and CPI source; use real CPI series not guesses.
topics: House price vs wages 1985 vs now
Cost of a loaf of bread over time
Minimum wage vs rent over time

us_vs_uk.name: US vs UK economy
us_vs_uk.desc: The big US vs UK economy comparison for the current period. At MOST once a month, only as an occasional special.
us_vs_uk.verify: Same period and units for both; convert currencies at a stated rate; GDP per person in PPP and nominal if both used.
topics: US vs UK economy this year (as of October)
US vs UK inflation and interest rates

where_tax_goes.name: Where does the tax go?
where_tax_goes.desc: Government budget split as a flow chart or donut: where each £/$ of tax goes.
where_tax_goes.verify: Latest published budget year; state it.
topics: Where each £1 of UK tax goes
Where each $1 of US federal tax goes
Who pays the most income tax in the UK
Where each £1 of VAT comes from

wealth_gap.name: Wealth and inequality
wealth_gap.verify: Define wealth vs income; state year.
topics: Top 1% share of wealth in 10 countries
Billionaire wealth vs a country's GDP

biggest_companies.name: Biggest companies / rankings
biggest_companies.desc: Ranked lists with bold bars: biggest companies, richest countries, largest economies.
forms: bar race snapshot with then vs now
sources: companiesmarketcap-style public market cap data via Yahoo Finance
biggest_companies.verify: State the date of market caps; use a single date for all.

trend.name: Trending now (economic)
trend.desc: A card on a genuinely trending, economically relevant topic (viral news, market event, policy shock, viral claim). ONLY if the topic is clearly trending today (several major outlets cover it) and the data can be verified. Otherwise do not use this series.
trend.verify: Fact-check the claim itself. If a viral claim is false, make the card about the real numbers. No speculation, no politics-as-opinion.
